content.title: About
content.content: Fat‑free mayonnaise is a dressing made from water, plant proteins, vinegar, mustard and flavorings. It retains the characteristic creamy taste of traditional mayo while containing minimal fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fat‑free mayo is often used to lower the calorie content of dishes without sacrificing flavor.
It may contain microscopic emulsifiers that stabilize the small amount of oil present.
In some countries it is marketed as a “healthier” alternative, though it can contain added sugars and preservatives.
The texture is usually thinner than that of classic mayonnaise.

items.title: Low Calorie Content
items.content: Fat‑free mayo provides far fewer calories than regular mayo, helping with energy balance control.

items.title: No Saturated Fats
items.content: The absence of saturated fats makes it more suitable for people monitoring cholesterol levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Formulations often include riboflavin (B2) and pyridoxine (B6), which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Additive Content
items.content: To improve taste and texture, artificial sweeteners, preservatives and flavor enhancers may be used.

items.title: Low Fat Satiety
items.content: Lack of fat can reduce satiety, potentially leading to larger portion consumption.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Some recipes contain mustard or soy protein, which are common allergens.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Fat‑free mayonnaise works well as a salad dressing, sandwich spread, sauce base, and in marinades. It can replace regular mayo in recipes that require a creamy texture while keeping calories low.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated after opening, sealed tightly, and use within 7‑10 days. Discard if the smell or consistency changes.
